title: Redis Persistence
subtitle: RDB snapshots vs AOF and hybrid persistence

content.text: Redis offers two persistence mechanisms: RDB (periodic snapshots) and AOF (append-only file of every write command).

content.code:
# RDB snapshot every 60 seconds if at least 1 key changed
save 60 1
dbfilename dump.rdb

# AOF
appendonly yes
appendfsync everysec

# Hybrid (recommended)
aof-use-rdb-preamble yes

content.definition: A point-in-time snapshot of the dataset. Fast to load on restart but may lose the last few minutes of writes.
Logs every write command. Minimal data loss but larger files and slower startup.

questions.question: Which persistence mode has the least data loss?
questions.explanation: AOF with always fsync writes to disk on every command — zero data loss but slowest.

faq.q: Can I use both RDB and AOF?
faq.a: Yes. The recommended setup is hybrid persistence: AOF with an RDB preamble. Use aof-use-rdb-preamble yes.
